title: O, Still Trust on, If in the Heart
description: O, Still Trust on, If in the Heart in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 299, “Not Faithless, But Believing”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, still trust on, if in the heart A ho-ly in-spi-ra-tion rest, Though pain-ful be the cho-sen part, With doubts, and fears, and cares op-prest! O, shrink not, broth-ers, though Christ's call De-mand our youth, our strength, our all!

lines: O, still trust on, if in the heart
Though painful be the chosen part,
With doubts, and fears, and cares opprest!
O, shrink not, brothers, though Christ's call
Demand our youth, our strength, our all!
No offering is made in vain;
Some human soul shall feel our love;
E'en weary hours of toil and pain
Shall help to lift our souls above:
And may our recompense be given,
In leading many souls to heaven!
And still trust on! with trembling hand,
'Tis ours a little seed to sow;
It springs at the divine command, —
Shall, if God will, to ripeness grow;
Beauty and fragrance it shall bring,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
